## Goal

**User story:** As a balance engineer, I want an executable contract (failing tests) for the two level-scaling axes before any production code exists, so the curves, rounding rules and cap behaviour are pinned before implementation.

This is the test-first item for the `src/core/levelScaling.ts` module and the `GameRules` scaling data (AC "Data-driven level-scaling curves" and the unit-test part of AC "Tests" of the parent item AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P).

## What to do

Create `src/core/levelScaling.test.ts` (new file) and extend `src/core/rules.test.ts` with tests that pin the agreed contract. These tests must **fail on pre-change HEAD** because neither the module nor the rules fields exist yet.

Curve contract to pin:

- `enemyCountMultiplier(level)`: `1.0` at level 1, `2.0` at level 10, linear in between (assert the exact formula value at level 5, e.g. `1 + (level - 1) * (1.0 / 9)`), monotonically non-decreasing across 1–10.
- `powerUpDropChance(level, rules)`: `0.18` at level 1 (equal to the exported `POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE`), `0.05` at level 10, monotonically non-increasing across 1–10, and `chance(10) <= 0.3 * chance(1)`.
- Extra Life proportionality: the small-asteroid Extra Life chance scales by the same ratio as the per-kill chance (`chance(level) / chance(1)`), so level 1 equals `rules.asteroidExtraLifeDropChance` exactly.
- Input clamping: levels below 1 clamp to 1, levels above the campaign maximum clamp to the maximum, and non-finite/non-integer inputs resolve to a documented clamped integer (no `NaN` output).
- Count application helper (`applyEnemyCountScaling` or the agreed equivalent): documented round-half-up rule, floor of 1, per-group safety cap of 200, `single`-formation groups left at exactly 1, and a level-1 identity transform (deep-equal input/output).
- Rules: the new scaling fields have documented defaults (1.0→2.0 multiplier, 0.18→0.05 drop chance), are clamped on load, and a legacy persisted blob without them loads with the defaults merged (backwards-compatible, no schema break).

## Acceptance Criteria

- New tests exist and fail on pre-change HEAD for the specified reason (module/rules fields absent); record the failure output in a comment on this item.
- Tests cover monotonicity, clamping, level-1 identity, rounding rule, `single` groups, the 200 cap, Extra Life proportionality and legacy rules-blob merging.
- No production code is modified by this item (tests only).
- Every test name states the behaviour it pins; no asserts without a stated reason.

- Parent AC traceability (verbatim from AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P): **Tests** — Unit tests cover curve monotonicity/clamping, count application (rounding, `single` groups, caps, L1 identity, seeded determinism), per-level drop chance, Extra Life proportionality and game↔gym parity. New tests fail on the pre-change code and pass after it.

## Key Files

- `src/core/levelScaling.test.ts` (new)
- `src/core/rules.test.ts`

## Dependencies

None. Blocks the level-scaling implementation item.

## Goal

**User story:** As a balance engineer, I want tests that pin how scaled enemy counts reach the campaign (static and sequenced) without breaking determinism or the existing campaign invariants, so the density change cannot silently reshape the authored campaign.

Test-first item for the parent AC "Enemy counts rise with level" (AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P).

## What to do

Add tests (in the existing wave test files, or a new `src/waves/scaledCampaign.test.ts`) that:

- Assert level-1 `LEVELS` wave groups are unchanged by the scaling path (deep-equal counts), so onboarding data stays byte-identical.

- Assert the shared helper is the only scaling implementation consumed by game and gym launch paths (parity seam), not a duplicated copy.

- Tests cover level-1 identity, level-10 growth, rounding, floor, cap, `single` groups, both campaign paths, same-seed determinism and no double scaling.

## Goal

**User story:** As a balance engineer, I want deterministic tests that prove the kill-time power-up supply falls with the campaign level, so the supply curve cannot regress unnoticed.

Test-first item for the parent AC "Power-up supply per enemy falls with level" (AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P).

## What to do

Extend `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` (and the rules tests where appropriate) with tests that:

- Force the scene RNG so the number of drops over N kills is exact and deterministic at level 1 (matches the current 0.18 rate) and at level 10 (matches 0.05, i.e. at most 30 % of the level-1 rate).
- Prove the level is resolved from the live campaign (`WaveManager.currentLevel()?.level`), i.e. after advancing a level the next kills use the new chance, and an unknown level falls back to level 1.
- Prove the small-asteroid Extra Life roll scales by the same ratio and is unchanged at level 1 (`rules.asteroidExtraLifeDropChance`).
- Prove drop types/weights, the mineral kill-drop rule and timed weapon/power-up effects are unaffected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New tests fail on pre-change HEAD (flat 0.18 roll for every level).
- Assertions are exact and seeded — no statistical/threshold flakiness.
- Coverage includes level 1 identity, level 10 endpoint, mid-run level advance, unknown-level fallback and Extra Life proportionality.
- No production code is modified by this item (tests only).

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`
- `src/core/rules.test.ts`

# We need an outer loop (AH-0MVNSSY9L001P1CC)

## Objective

**User story (producer).** As the producer, I want the region/home-world proposal
plus **two genuinely different** outer-loop candidates, each written up as a
decision-ready outline on the same footing, so that I can choose one and have it
written into the Game Design Document (GDD) with confidence.

**User story (player).** As a player, I want something to carry forward between
runs — a long-term goal and a sense that my play changes the world — so that
losing a run does not mean losing all progress, and so that beating the final
boss is a milestone on the way to winning rather than the end of everything.

## Users

- **Producer / designer (primary).** Chooses one of three outlined loops and owns
  the GDD write-up; needs comparable, honest outlines and a defensible ranking.
- **Player (arcade / bullet-hell fan).** Needs a reason to return after a lost
  run and a goal beyond a high score; wants progress that survives failure.
- **Developer / agent implementing the loop later.** Needs each outline to name
  the systems, seams and gym coverage so the chosen loop can be planned without
  re-deriving the design.

## Problem statement

The game has a strong **inner loop** (flying, dodging formations, destroying
enemies) and a functioning **middle loop** (per-run ship upgrading through
minerals → hold-full power-up choices → levelled weapons), but **no outer loop**:
nothing persists between runs except a leaderboard score, player settings and a
single run checkpoint. A death ends the run outright (GDD §4.6: "There is no
continue mechanic. Game over is final"), so long-term engagement rests entirely
on score chasing. The fiction ("pilot a resistance ship through a digital
underworld ruled by rogue AI") implies a war to be won, but the game currently
has no structure that represents winning it.

The producer has proposed one candidate outer loop (contested regions with a
home world to find and defend) and asked for **two other candidates** to be
brainstormed and outlined, after which the producer chooses one for the GDD.

## Deliverable

A single design-exploration document — `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — built
to the same standard as the existing research catalogues
(`docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md`, `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`):
selected candidates written up per-concept, a "considered but not selected"
section, and a selection recommendation. It is a **design document only**: no
gameplay code, no persistence schema changes and no new scenes are implemented
in this item.

The producer's choice is then written into the GDD as a follow-on work item; this
item ends at the candidate document, the comparison and the recommendation.

## Loop tiers used by the document

| Tier | Timescale | Definition in this game | Exists today? |
|------|-----------|-------------------------|---------------|
| **Inner** | Seconds | Flying, dodging, destroying enemies and formations within a wave | Yes (GDD §2.3–2.6) |
| **Middle** | Minutes (a run) | Ship upgrading: minerals → hold-full power-up/weapon choices, levelled effects, extra lives | Yes (GDD §4.4, §4.6) |
| **Outer** | Hours (a campaign / a season) | What the player carries **between** runs and what they are ultimately trying to achieve | **No** |

## Candidate A — Contested Regions / Home World (producer's proposal)

Recorded as proposed, not redesigned. Its outline must preserve every named
mechanic:

- Space is divided into **regions**; each region has an **AI aggression level**.
- The ship can **warp a limited distance** to adjacent regions.
- The goal is to find a region with **zero aggression** containing a **planet
  that can become home to the humans**.
- Having found it, the player must **defend all adjacent regions** against
  attack by aggressive AI.
- The player may leave their **fully upgraded ship** in a region with an **AI
  automated pilot** that defends that region.
- The player then returns home and **collects another ship with no upgrades**,
  and must go out again to make it strong enough to be left guarding another
  region.
- **Factional AI warfare** changes region strength over time: warring AI
  factions fight over a region and the winner leaves a stronger force there.
- **Win condition:** all regions have successfully defended against a massive AI
  onslaught, at which point the home world is safe and the game is won.

The outline must state its **minimal first slice** (the smallest version that
proves the loop is fun), because the full proposal is the largest of the three.

## Candidate B — Salvage Fleet (proposed direction, resource-persistent meta)

A **roguelite meta-progression** outer loop that leaves the map alone and
persists **player power** instead.

- Between runs the player spends **banked salvage** (minerals and mini-boss AI
  cores extracted at the existing checkpoint moments) in a persistent **hangar**
  to unlock hulls, starting weapons and permanent modifiers.
- Each run is a **deployment** flown in one chosen hull; losing the run forfeits
  that run's unbanked salvage but never the hangar.
- The outer goal is to assemble a fleet strong enough for a final assault run at
  maximum threat.
- Progression axis: **build/economy** (what the player owns), not territory.

## Candidate C — Signal Decode (proposed direction, knowledge-persistent meta)

A **campaign-mutating** outer loop where the thing that persists is
**information**.

- Mini-bosses and the boss drop **data fragments** that assemble a persistent
  codex revealing the origin of the AI and the "hellscape" it generates.
- Codex knowledge **mutates and unlocks the campaign** (new enemy behaviours,
  hellscape modifiers, shortcuts), and the final confrontation only becomes
  winnable once the core's rules have been decoded — the boss's phases are the
  codex's payoff.
- Progression axis: **knowledge and campaign variation**, not territory or
  currency.

## Required outline structure (every candidate)

1. **Fantasy / pitch** — one paragraph, in the game's fiction.
2. **Loop structure** — moment-to-moment → run → meta, with an explicit
   statement of *what carries between runs*.
3. **States** — win, lose, partial progress and what a bad run still advances.
4. **New systems** required (named, with rough size).
5. **Reuse of existing systems** — checkpoint (`src/core/checkpointStore.ts`),
   minerals/power-up levels, `Leaderboard`, difficulty curves
   (`src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`), mini-boss rewards, bot/attract mode.
6. **Persistence and save model** — a sketch `localStorage` payload under
   §6.6 rules (defensive parse, no backend) with migration note.
7. **Session shape** — target run length and hours-to-win.
8. **UI / scene surface** — which new screens or menu entries are needed.
9. **Gym testability and the bot** — how its gameplay additions can be exercised
   in a gym (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity rule) and how attract mode can complete
   or avoid stalling on the outer loop.
10. **Pillar impact** — which current GDD pillars it changes (e.g. "no continue,
    game over is final", the single final boss), stated explicitly.
11. **Effort and risk** — sized honestly, with the failure modes that would make
    the loop unfun.
12. **Minimal first slice** — the smallest shippable version.

A **comparison table** then ranks all candidates on: fit with the existing
pilots-in-a-digital-hell fiction, reuse of shipped systems, new-system cost,
persistence complexity, session length fit, legibility of progress to the player,
gym/bot testability, and risk of trivialising or gutting the shipped campaign —
followed by an explicit **recommendation with rationale** and why the others rank
lower. A "Considered but not selected" section records further ideas (e.g. an
arcade-style tiered mutator ladder, a pure daily-seed challenge ladder) with a
one-line deferral reason each.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Deliverable exists and frames the problem.** `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`
   exists, opens with the inner/middle/outer tier definitions above and the
   comparison criteria, and states that it is design-only.
2. **Candidate A is complete and faithful.** Candidate A is written up with all
   twelve required sections and preserves every mechanic listed in *Candidate A*
   above (regions, limited warp, per-region aggression, zero-aggression home
   region with a habitable planet, defence of adjacent regions, autonomous-pilot
   ship hand-off, unupgraded replacement ship, faction warfare, all-regions-held
   win). No proposed mechanic is silently dropped, altered or merged.
3. **Two additional candidates, materially distinct.** Candidates B and C each
   carry all twelve required sections and each names *what persists between
   runs* differently from Candidate A and from each other; each is justified
   against at least one named design pillar or fiction element.
4. **Decision-ready comparison.** The document contains a comparison table across
   the agreed criteria, an explicit recommendation with rationale, and a ranked
   justification for why the two non-recommended candidates rank lower.
5. **Alternatives recorded.** A "Considered but not selected" section lists at
   least two further outer-loop ideas with a one-line deferral reason each.
6. **Docs guard test.** A vitest docs-guard test (convention:

# Make Phase Shift and wormhole-emergence effects unmistakable

## Problem statement

The improved Phase Shift / wormhole-emergence treatment shipped under
AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S (commits 4267a534, 4b407b66, eafc45b6, c84c1a99, 5b5877e4) is
technically complete and audited, but **the producer reports it is still not
noticeable enough — the effect must be unmistakable**. The intent of the original
epic ("instantly obvious that they are not in their usual state") is therefore not
yet satisfied in practice, even though every written acceptance criterion passed.

Producer feedback (2026-10-25, verbatim): *"These effects are not noticeable
enough, needs to be unmistakable."*

## Users

- **Player (primary):** "As a player, the instant my ship phases out — or enemies
  start materialising out of the wormhole — I want to *know* without looking for
  it. Not a tint I have to hunt for: an unmistakable event."
- **Player (defensive read):** "As a player relying on the automatic Phase Shift, I
  want the activation to read like a system event (a hit, a pulse, a distortion),
  not a subtle colour shift, so I can trust it and time my flying."
- **Developer / maintainer:** "As a developer, I want whatever stronger treatment we
  choose to live once in the shared VFX layer, stay toggleable per layer, and keep
  the gyms and the game pixel-identical."

## Current state (what shipped, and why it reads as subtle)

Screen-wide Phase Shift (`src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts`):

| Layer | Current value |
|---|---|
| Dim overlay | dark blue 0x0a1a33, alpha 0.22 |
| Chromatic split | cyan 0x33ffee / red 0xff3355, **alpha 0.20**, base offset **6 px** (+/-1.5 px, 1.6 s) |
| Alpha flicker | 3 Hz, 25 % depth |
| Colour pulse | 0.75 -> 1.0 cross-fade |
| Activation burst | alpha 0.35 at +/-12 px, 200 ms fade |
| Camera shake | **deliberately none** (producer decision: it read like death juice) |

Per-enemy emergence (`src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` `updateEnemyShimmer`):
ripple burst +0.06 scale / +0.15 alpha over 200 ms, then alpha flicker 0.55-0.85 at
3 Hz, scale pulse 4 %, additive-bloom colour pulse (Phaser 4 `Container`/`Graphics`
have no Tint).

Wormhole ring (`attachWormholeRing`): 0xd9b3ff, r 52 px, 3 px stroke, alpha 0.45,
yoyo scale 0.9-1.15 every 900 ms.

Diagnosis of the shortfall (to be confirmed with the producer): every layer is a
**low-alpha translucent tint at screen-wide scale**, and translucency over a busy
bullet-hell background is perceptually weak. "Unmistakable" most likely needs
*high-contrast, structural* change — distortion, a hard flash, silhouettes, motion —
not just larger alpha values.

## Candidate approaches (producer to choose / amend)

**A — Bigger same-technique (lowest risk, no new rendering technique).**
Split alpha 0.20 -> ~0.45 and offset 6 -> ~14 px; burst alpha 0.35 -> ~0.70 at
+/-28 px over ~320 ms; add a short full-screen brightness flash on activation
(distinct palette from the death flash); add cyan edge/vignette bands during phase
(the defeat-screen vignette technique) so the *frame* changes, not just the objects;
per-enemy alpha flicker range widened (e.g. 0.25-1.0) plus a stroked silhouette
outline per emerging enemy; wormhole ring radius/alpha raised with an open shockwave.

**B — Real screen-space distortion via Phaser camera post-FX (highest impact).**
Use the engine's built-in post-FX pipelines on the main camera while phased: a
short displacement/pixelate wobble on the activation edge, then a sustained subtle
`Bloom`/`Glow` + gentle `Barrel`/`Displacement` wobble, all driven from the same
tunables. This is the genuine "glitch" read and is far more visible than alpha
tints. Caveats: the original epic explicitly scoped shader/render-to-texture work
out; needs a WebGL check + a headless-safe fallback, a measurable perf check, and a
canvas-renderer degradation path. Phaser post-FX state must also be torn down
exactly on the falling edge.

**C — Combination (recommended by the agent, producer decides).**
A for the player + wormhole (cheap, robust) **plus** B's activation-edge distortion
burst only (a ~150-250 ms pixelate/displacement hit), so the *event* is unmistakable
while the *sustained* state stays comfortable.

## Constraints

- **Gym<->game parity** (AGENTS.md): the behaviour lives once in `src/vfx/*` and the
  shared spawn path; `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel` and the combat gyms
  consume the same code. The duplicate-body guard and the gym-parity docs assertion
  must stay green.
- **No camera shake** unless the producer explicitly reverses that decision. (The
  regression test asserting "never shakes" currently encodes it.) If a shake-free
  "punch" is wanted, prefer camera **zoom** punch or post-FX over shake.
- **Seizure safety:** a genuinely unmistakable effect must still avoid rapid strobe.
  If flicker frequency rises, cap it (~<=3-4 Hz for sustained layers) and add an
  explicit accessibility toggle; a reduce-motion option remains a separate item.
- **Per-layer toggles and pure params model** are retained (`PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*`,
  `ENEMY_SHIMMER_ENABLE_*`, `WORMHOLE_RING_ENABLE`, pure `resolve*Params()`).
- **Headless-safe:** no-op without a Phaser render context; unit tests stay
  deterministic.
- **Performance-neutral to near-neutral:** no per-frame allocations; post-FX, if
  chosen, needs a measured cost check on the existing target hardware.
- **Visual distinctness from player-death juice** must be preserved and asserted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Player activation edge is an aggressive, structural glitch: a short camera-filter distortion burst plus a full-screen phase flash plus a wider chromatic surge.
- Player sustained state stays continuously obvious but soft: pulsing vivid split, cyan edge vignette bands, gentle sustained camera filter, no camera shake.
- Exact teardown: the falling edge removes every overlay, tween and camera filter, restoring the camera filter list with no residual state or duplicate layer.
- WebGL capability probe with graceful fallback: filter layers apply only when supported, otherwise degrading to overlay-only layers without throwing.
- Per-enemy emergence is unmistakable per entity: outline silhouette, stronger ripple burst, widened alpha flicker, fully restored when growth ends, no screen-wide overlay.
- Wormhole read: a brighter larger pulsing ring plus a one-shot open shockwave, tracked in wormholeEffects and fully cleared when the wormhole closes.
- Distinctness and parity preserved: visually distinct from player-death juice, never shakes the camera, gym-game parity guards green, headless no-op safe.
- Tests and docs: unit tests cover every new layer, teardown, fallback and the no-shake regression; GDD section 7.2 and code comments document all tunables; the full suite passes.

## Acceptance notes (detail per criterion)

1. **Activation edge (aggressive).** Rising edge fires, in the same frame: a ~150-250 ms camera-filter distortion burst (pixelate + barrel/displacement wobble), a full-screen flash in a phase-shift palette (never the player-death flash palette), and the widened/stronger chromatic-surge overlay pair. Every magnitude is an exported tunable; every layer has its own `PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*` toggle.
2. **Sustained state (soft).** Split alpha/offset raised and slowly oscillating, cyan edge/vignette band layer, gentle sustained filter layer; sustained flicker capped at <=3-4 Hz for seizure safety; no camera shake.
3. **Teardown detail.** A second expiry, a scene `SHUTDOWN` or a re-activation cycle leaves no residual tint, no leaked filter controller, no duplicated layer; pre-existing unrelated camera filters survive untouched.
4. **Fallback detail.** Renderer probe checks the WebGL renderer type and the camera filter list; unsupported renderers get the overlay-only layers with no error storm (headless/canvas tests exercise this path).
5. **Emergence detail.** Driven from the shared spawn path (`updateSpawnAnimation` -> `updateEnemyShimmer`) over the whole `ENEMY_GROWTH_DURATION`; the entity's own alpha/scale/blend state is fully restored when growth ends.
6. **Wormhole detail.** One ring and one shockwave per wormhole; tweens stopped before destroy; registry cleared on close.
7. **Distinctness detail.** The no-shake regression test is retained; the duplicate-body guard (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the gym-parity docs assertion stay green.
8. **Docs detail.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` section 7.2 plus JSDoc on every new exported constant and helper.

## Producer decisions (2026-10-25)## Producer decisions (2026-10-25)

- **Q1 = C** — combination: approach A (bigger same-technique + frame-level flash/vignette/silhouette) everywhere, **plus** approach B's screen-space distortion for the player path.
- **Q2 = iii** — aggressive on the activation edge, soft for the sustained state.
- **Q3 = no shake** — the no-camera-shake decision stands; the "punch" comes from post-FX/flash layers only. The existing regression test stays.
- **Q4 = ship and iterate** — the epic AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S is **not** held: no dependency edge from the epic to this item; it releases through the normal dev->main gate and this item improves the effect afterwards.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Which approach?** (A) bigger same-technique only; (B) real screen-space post-FX distortion for the player path; (C) combination.
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-25): **C**. Rationale: keep the robust overlay/vignette/silhouette work everywhere and add a genuine distortion read for the player's activation.
- **Q2 — How far may intensity go?** (i) comfortably strong; (ii) aggressive/startling; (iii) aggressive activation edge, soft sustained.
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-25): **iii**. Rationale: the *event* must be unmistakable; the *state* must stay comfortable for the whole phase duration.
- **Q3 — Revisit the no-shake rule?** (i) keep no-shake, use post-FX/flash instead; (ii) allow a short low-intensity shake on the activation edge only.
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-25): **no shake**. Rationale: preserves the established distinctness from player-death juice.
- **Q4 — Release hold for the epic AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S?** hold its release until this lands, or ship and iterate.
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-25): **ship and iterate**. No blocking edge is wired from the epic to this item.

## Technical feasibility note (verified before planning)

Phaser 4.2.1 exposes camera filters (`camera.filters.internal` / `.external`):
`addPixelate`, `addBarrel`, `addGlow`, `addVignette`, `addBlur`, `addParallelFilters`
(bloom), `addDisplacement`, `addColorMatrix`. They are **WebGL only**, so the driver
must probe `scene.game.renderer.type` / `camera.filters` and degrade to the
overlay-only layers otherwise. No post-FX is used anywhere in `src/` today, so this is
a new (but engine-supported) technique.

## Constraints

- **Gym<->game parity** (AGENTS.md): the behaviour lives once in `src/vfx/*` and the
  shared spawn path; `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel` and the combat gyms
  consume the same code. The duplicate-body guard and the gym-parity docs assertion
  must stay green.
- **No camera shake** unless the producer explicitly reverses that decision. (The
  regression test asserting "never shakes" currently encodes it.) If a shake-free
  "punch" is wanted, prefer camera **zoom** punch or post-FX over shake.
- **Seizure safety:** a genuinely unmistakable effect must still avoid rapid strobe.
  If flicker frequency rises, cap it (~<=3-4 Hz for sustained layers) and add an
  explicit accessibility toggle; a reduce-motion option remains a separate item.
- **Per-layer toggles and pure params model** are retained (`PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*`,
  `ENEMY_SHIMMER_ENABLE_*`, `WORMHOLE_RING_ENABLE`, pure `resolve*Params()`).
- **Headless-safe:** no-op without a Phaser render context; unit tests stay
  deterministic.
- **Performance-neutral to near-neutral:** no per-frame allocations; post-FX, if
  chosen, needs a measured cost check on the existing target hardware.
- **Visual distinctness from player-death juice** must be preserved and asserted.

## Acceptance Criteria (draft — finalise after producer answers Q1-Q3)

- **Unmistakable activation read (player).** On the `isPhased` rising edge the
  treatment produces a structural, high-contrast change (not merely a tint): the
  chosen mechanism (A/B/C) fires within the same frame and is perceptible against a
  busy background in a manual play check; magnitudes exported as tunables with
  per-layer toggles.
- **Unmistakable sustained read (player).** While phased, the state remains
  continuously obvious for the whole duration (chosen sustained layer(s) from A
  and/or B), with the no-camera-shake guarantee intact and every layer torn down on
  the falling edge (no residual tint or residual post-FX state).
- **Unmistakable emergence read (enemies).** Each emerging enemy is individually
  obvious as "not solid yet" across its whole `ENEMY_GROWTH_DURATION` window, driven
  from the shared spawn path; the entity's own render state is fully restored when
  growth ends; no screen-wide overlay on the emergence path.
- **Wormhole read.** The open wormhole is clearly the source of the emergence (ring
  and/or column strengthened per the chosen approach), tracked in the existing
  `wormholeEffects` registry and fully cleared on close.
- **No regressions.** Death juice stays visually distinct; the no-shake regression
  holds (unless the producer reverses it, in which case it is updated deliberately);
  gym<->game parity guards pass; headless no-op tests pass.
- **Tests and docs.** Unit tests cover the new tunables/toggles, the new
  layers/mechanism creation + teardown (including post-FX teardown if chosen), and
  the no-shake and headless guarantees. `docs/Game Design Document.md` section 7.2
  and the code comments are updated with the final magnitudes. The full project test
  suite passes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) — magnitudes, new layers, optional
  camera post-FX driver.
- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) — per-enemy treatment, wormhole ring.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — shared driver (post-FX needs a camera).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts` — consume the shared helpers only (no new behaviour).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` section 7.2 — final treatment + tunables.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S** (completed, audited, awaiting release) — the epic that
  delivered the current treatment. This item is `discovered-from:AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S`.
  The producer must decide whether the epic's release is held until this lands.
- AH-0MVD2MXAB004K0V4 — player phase-shift juice (vivid split + burst + shimmer).

## Risks and assumptions

  contrast and faster flicker. Mitigation: cap sustained flicker, keep the aggressive

  needs canvas fallback, exact teardown, and a perf measurement. Mitigation: fall

- **Risk: parity drift** — mitigated by implementing once in the shared VFX layer;
  guards enforce it.
- **Assumption:** the producer's "unmistakable" means *perceptually unavoidable*,
  not necessarily *physically larger* — the chosen mechanism is a producer decision
  (Q1-Q3 above).

# Bot tuning scene is not using the same gameplay objects as the main game

## Problem statement

Gym scenes are the canonical parity reference for the shipped game, yet the
level-launch gym path (`GymLevel`, which `GymBotTuning` extends) carries its own
inline wave-spawn implementation that has drifted from `PlayScene`. A designer
tuning the bot therefore watches enemies that do **not** behave as they do in
play, which invalidates the tuning signal the gym exists to provide.

## Findings from repo investigation (intake, 2026-10-27)

The reported symptom is real and is one of several divergences in the same spawn
seam:

1. **Phasers spawn in a line then snap to their ring (reported bug).**
   `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1647`) and
   `GymFormationScene` (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts:1755`) both
   resolve an orbital entity's wormhole-transit destination through the entity's
   live `formationSlot()` seam (AH-0MVEXVME1004SIIS). `GymLevel.spawnWave`
   (`src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts:299`) does not: its resolver returns the grid
   slot (`startX + driftX + col * spacingX`), so Phasers transit to a straight
   line and then snap onto the orbit when the spawn window ends. Because
   `GymBotTuning extends GymLevel` (`src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts:149`), the
   bot-tuning gym reproduces exactly the symptom the producer reported.
   Regression coverage exists for `PlayScene`
   (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:6697`) and `GymFodderEnemies`
   (`src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.test.ts:396`) but **not** for
   `GymLevel`/`GymBotTuning`.

2. **Launched-level enemies never fire.** `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` assigns
   `entity.shootEnabled = spawn.shootEnabled`; `GymLevel.spawnWave` never
   assigns it, and `BaseEnemy._shootEnabled` defaults to `false`
   (`src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts:97`), so every `tryFire*` method returns nothing.
   Campaign levels 4+ carry `shootEnabled: true`
   (`src/waves/Formations.ts:157`), so a level launched from the curve editor or
   played in the bot-tuning gym is silently non-threatening. `GymLevel`'s own
   tests work around this by setting `victim.shootEnabled = true` by hand
   (`src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.test.ts:599`), which is itself evidence of the gap.

3. **March formations do not march.** `PlayScene` keeps a rigid `marchState`
   block and re-anchors march spawns (`_resetMarchFormation`,
   `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1737`); `GymLevel` has only horizontal `driftX`.
   Campaign levels 2–10 contain `march` groups
   (`src/waves/Formations.ts:381-424`), so the launched block renders as a
   static line instead of the stepping/dropping block the game shows.

4. **The transit resolver is copied three times.** Each spawn site inlines the
   same non-trivial logic ("autonomous-mover exemption → orbital-slot branch →
   live slot / offset fallback"). The repo-wide duplicate-body guard
   (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS`)
   does not cover this seam, which is why the third copy could drift unnoticed.
   `GymLevel` also keeps a legacy in-place spawn path used when no wormhole
   origin is supplied — dead for gameplay but still a second code path to keep
   honest.

5. **Divergences that must be preserved (already documented).** `GymPlayer`'s
   obstacle course, `GymWeapons`' AOE training targets, the flat supply cadence
   in `GymFormationScene`-derived gyms, gym-only HUD/tuning panels and the
   absence of run telemetry are intentional and recorded in
   `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 and `docs/BALANCING.md`. The
   fix must not "unify" these away.

## Users and example user stories

- **Bot-tuning designer (primary):** "As a designer tuning the bot in
  `GymBotTuning`, I want the enemies I watch to spawn, transit, march and fire
  exactly as they do in the shipped game, so the tuning I save transfers to the
  attract demo and recordings."
- **Gameplay developer:** "As a developer landing a spawn/formation fix in
  `PlayScene`, I want the gyms to consume the same seam, so I cannot leave a gym
  behind without the test suite failing."
- **Level/curve designer:** "As a designer launching a campaign level from the
  curve editor, I want the launched level to be a faithful preview of the
  shipped level."

## Existing state

- Three spawn implementations: `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` (game),
  `GymFormationScene` (formation gyms), `GymLevel.spawnWave` (level/bot-tuning
  gyms). Only the first two honour the `formationSlot` seam.
- Spawn presentation (`startSpawnAnimation`, wormhole open/close, spawn
  protection) is already shared via `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`; what diverges is
  the **destination resolver**, the per-enemy `shootEnabled` hand-off and the
  march block.
- Gym↔game parity coverage is extensive for combat, drops, movement, boss
  motion and projectile lifecycle, but has no coverage for the start-of-wave
  spawn presentation on the level-launch path.
- The capture/scripted-scene seam (`src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts`) is already
  consumed by `GymFormationScene` and `GymLevel` only, and the scene registry
  (`scripts/capture-scenes.mjs`) already lists every `Gym<Name>` as capturable
  except the parameterised `GymFodderEnemies`/`GymLevel`.

## Desired change

1. Extract the wormhole-transit destination resolution into **one** shared
   helper under `src/scenes/core/` and make all four spawn sites
   (`PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel`, `GymBoss` minions) consume it,
   so the orbital-slot seam, the autonomous-mover exemption and the live-slot
   tracking can no longer drift.
2. Propagate the wave's per-enemy `shootEnabled` (and the formation RNG) through
   the `GymLevel` spawn path exactly as `PlayScene` does.
3. Bring the march block to the level-launch path (or consume the shared march
   state) so launched march waves step and drop as they do in the game.
4. Register the new seam in the duplicate-body guard and add cross-scene
   equivalence tests that boot `PlayScene` and `GymLevel`/`GymBotTuning` with the
   same seeded orbital/march wave and assert identical spawn trajectories and
   identical fire cadence.
5. Sweep **every** gym scene (`src/scenes/gym/`, including the generic
   `GymFormationScene` and the level/bot-tuning path) against `PlayScene` for
   enabled-object parity and record the result in a single parity matrix. **Fix
   every real divergence found in this item** (each with a test), rather than
   deferring them; documented, intentional divergences stay, with their reason
   recorded in the matrix.
6. Adopt the scripted-scene `setup` seam in **every** gym in this item: each gym
   applies the shared `applySceneSetup` applier and exposes whatever
   scene-specific scenario parameters it needs (enemy roster, formation, level,
   toggles) through the capture scene config, so any gym can be driven from
   `examples/scenes.json` and recorded. Extend the config validation and the
   `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` / parameterised-scene contracts accordingly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — Booting `PlayScene` and `GymLevel` (and therefore `GymBotTuning`) with the same seeded orbital wave produces the same per-frame transit target for every Phaser: each frame's destination equals the entity's live `formationSlot()`, and no enemy is ever placed on a straight line then snapped to the ring. Verified by a cross-scene equivalence test that fails on the pre-change code (red-before / green-after).
- [ ] AC2 — A launched wave with `shootEnabled: true` fires in `GymLevel` / `GymBotTuning` at the same cadence and bullet speed as the same wave in `PlayScene` (shared dispatcher, real scene clock). Verified by a parity test, not a hand-set `shootEnabled` in the test.
- [ ] AC3 — A launched `march` wave steps/drops in the gym exactly as the game's block does for the same `dt` sequence. Verified by a parity test.
- [ ] AC4 — The spawn-transit destination logic is defined exactly **once** repo-wide, is registered in `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS`, and every spawn site (`PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel`, `GymBoss`) resolves to it; the duplicate-body guard fails if a copy is re-introduced.
- [ ] AC5 — A gym↔game parity matrix document records, for **every** gym scene under `src/scenes/gym/` (including the generic `GymFormationScene` and the level/bot-tuning path), which shipped gameplay objects it runs, whether it inherits the shipped start-of-wave/combat code, and — where it diverges — the reason. Every real divergence identified by the sweep is **fixed in this item** with a regression test; retained divergences are only those already documented as intentional and each is re-justified in the matrix.
- [ ] AC6 — Every gym applies the shared scripted-scene `setup` seam and exposes its scenario parameters through the capture scene config, so any gym can be launched and recorded from `examples/scenes.json`; the scene-config validator rejects unsupported/parameterised targets with a clear error, and the `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` registry contract and its pinning test are updated.
- [ ] AC7 — `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 (and `AGENTS.md` § Game Architecture Conventions where the rule text changes) explain the shared spawn seam and point at the parity matrix; the docs guard test still passes.
- [ ] AC8 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries (including the scripted-scene/gym capture documentation).
- [ ] AC9 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No balance changes. Behavioural differences introduced by this item must be a
  *fix toward* the game's behaviour, except where the producer explicitly asks
  for a new gym capability (scripted-scene setup, AC6).
- Must not "fix" documented intentional divergences (obstacle course, AOE
  practice targets, flat formation-gym supply cadence, gym HUD); each must keep
  its documented reason.
- Must not regress the automation that consumes the gyms: the capture CLI and
  `sceneSetup` appliers, Watch Demo / demo mode, the bot-tuning store, and the
  `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` registry contract.
- Scope is deliberately broad (producer direction: sweep and fix all in this
  item). If the sweep uncovers a divergence that cannot be fixed without a
  separate design decision, record it as a blocker with evidence on this item
  rather than silently expanding the design.
- The item is expected to be decomposed into child items at the plan stage
  (shared seam, spawn-parity fixes, gym sweep, scripted-scene adoption, docs);
  the ACs above are the whole-item contract.
- The reported symptom must be reproducible before the fix and demonstrably
  fixed after it (red-before / green-after per repo convention).
- Implementation runs in the item's own worktree per `AGENTS.md`.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/spawnTransit.ts` — **new** shared destination-resolver seam

## Related work

# Orbital Strike does nothing

## Problem statement

The **Orbital Strike** power-up is functionally wired but reads to the player as
doing nothing: it produces **no sound at all** and reuses the generic Smart Bomb
AOE ring instead of an orbital bolt, so nothing about it says "an orbital strike
just happened". Worse, in the two most common situations the bolt is **silently
consumed with zero feedback** — no VFX, no SFX, no damage.

## Users

As a **player**, I want picking up an Orbital Strike to produce an unmistakable
event — a bolt falling from the sky onto the target with its own sound — so that
I can tell the power-up is working, and so that the permanent (hold-full) reward
is worth the choice.

As a **player**, I do not want a pickup wasted silently when it is collected
while no enemy is alive; I want the strike to land on the next target (or be
clearly signalled as unused).

## Existing state (repo research)

The power-up is **not** dead code — the damage path exists and is tested. What is
missing is the *feedback layer* plus two silent-failure paths.

1. **State + decision (working).** `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect` sets
   `_strikePulsePending = true` for a field pickup and `_strikePermanent = true`
   + a pulse timer for a hold-full reward (`src/powerups/effects.ts:644`).
   `EffectsRegistry.updateStrike(dt)` (`src/powerups/effects.ts:1241`) returns
   `true` exactly once for a queued pickup and then once per
   `strikeInterval()` (`max(10, 30 − 2×level)` s) for the permanent reward.
2. **Shared detection (working).** `CombatCoreScene._updateOrbitalStrike`
   (`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts:1655`) is called from `_tickPlayer`
   (`:878`) and forwards to the `onOrbitalStrike(damage)` hook, so the game and
   every gym run one implementation.
3. **Application (working, but visually generic).**
   `CombatScene.onOrbitalStrike` (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:642`) picks the
   live enemy nearest the ship, then spawns
   `spawnNovaRing(..., ORBITAL_STRIKE_RADIUS = 40, ORBITAL_STRIKE_COLOR = 0x9ffcff)`
   plus `spawnBulletImpact(...)` and applies `damageEnemyViaAoe(target, damage)`.
   That is **the same nova-ring helper and colour family as the Smart Bomb
   pulse** (`onSmartBombPulse`, `CombatScene.ts:673`) — there is no descending
   bolt, no target marker, no telegraph, no screen flash/shake. The ring lasts
   `NOVA_RING_DURATION = 0.5` s (`src/vfx/aoeEffect.ts:25`), so it is easy to miss
   entirely during play.
4. **No SFX exists.** `src/audio/effects.ts` exports **no** orbital-strike cue
   and `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` (66 cues) has **no** strike entry. The
   `onOrbitalStrike` body makes no `play*` call. The unrelated Missile-Command
   **hazard** entity (`src/entities/OrbitalStrike.ts`) borrows
   `playScoutAdvanceCue` (`docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md:94`), which is
   why the hazard is audible and the power-up is silent.
5. **Silent-waste path A — no target.** `onOrbitalStrike` returns early when no
   live enemy is found (`CombatScene.ts:646`), but `updateStrike` has **already**
   cleared `_strikePulsePending`. A pickup collected between waves is therefore
   consumed with literally no effect: "it does nothing at all".
6. **Silent-waste path B — no player.** `_updateOrbitalStrike` does not guard on
   a live player; `onOrbitalStrike` does. Same silent consumption.
7. **Weak readout.** The HUD shows a `strike` row **only** while the strike is
   permanent (`src/ui/HUD.ts:523`) and never shows the time to the next bolt, so
   even an armed permanent strike looks inert.
8. **Damage is often invisible.** `strikeDamage()` is `1` hit at level 1
   (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts:979`), so a bolt on a multi-HP enemy removes
   one pip and on a 1-HP grunt is indistinguishable from an ordinary bullet kill.

## Desired change

Give Orbital Strike a distinct, legible identity and remove the silent failures:

- A **descending orbital bolt** (beam/column from off-screen top down to the
  target) ending in a bright impact flash — its own VFX module, not the Smart
  Bomb ring.
- A **new dedicated SFX cue** (`aihell-orbital-strike`, baked WAV), played at the
  bolt's impact.
- **No silent consumption**: a queued bolt with no live target (or no live
  player) is **retained** and fired on the first valid frame rather than being
  discarded.
- The HUD `strike` row shows the countdown to the next bolt for a permanent
  strike.

> Scope confirmed by the producer (2026-10-28): this work item covers the
> **power-up** only; the Missile-Command `orbital-strike` hazard is out of scope
> except for non-regression (AC7).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Distinct visual identity.** A strike (field pickup or permanent pulse)
   renders a descending bolt from the top of the play area onto the target plus
   an impact flash, through a new VFX module in `src/vfx/`, and the visual is
   demonstrably distinct from the Smart Bomb pulse (different shape/composition,
   not just a recoloured `spawnNovaRing`), asserted by unit tests on the module.
2. **Dedicated audio cue.** A new `playOrbitalStrikeSound` cue exists in
   `src/audio/effects.ts`, backed by a **new** ToneForge recipe
   (`aihell-orbital-strike`, baked WAV built via `scripts/build-audio.sh`),
   registered in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`, and played by the shared strike
   path; `src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts` and `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts`
   stay green.
3. **No silent waste.** A strike that resolves while no live enemy (or no live
   player) is present is **not** lost: the queued bolt is **retained** and lands
   on the first frame with a valid target. A regression test drives a pickup with
   no live enemy and asserts the bolt subsequently lands on the next live enemy.
   At most one bolt is retained (a permanent strike simply resumes its interval)
   so a long enemy-free gap cannot bank a volley.
4. **Damage path unchanged.** The bolt still applies `strikeDamage()` hits to the
   nearest live enemy through `damageEnemyViaAoe`, and still depletes enemy force
   fields through the shared `takeDamage()` seam —
   `src/scenes/core/enemyForceFieldDamageSources.test.ts` and
   `src/scenes/core/powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts` stay green.
5. **Gym↔game parity.** The VFX/SFX and the no-silent-waste behaviour live once
   in the shared core (`src/scenes/core/`) and are consumed by `PlayScene` and
   every gym; `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (duplicate-body
   guard) and a gym parity test in `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts`
   stay green, and the strike is observable in the gym.
6. **HUD countdown.** A permanent strike's HUD row shows a live countdown
   (`next in Ns`) to the next bolt, asserted by a HUD test.
7. **Hazard reviewed, not regressed.** The unrelated Missile-Command
   `orbital-strike` hazard (`src/entities/OrbitalStrike.ts`) is confirmed
   unaffected by this change; its suite (`src/entities/OrbitalStrike.test.ts`,
   `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` §"Missile Command telegraphed orbital strike")
   stays green.
8. **Testing/validation.** Every acceptance criterion above is covered by an
   automated test that fails before the change and passes after it.
9. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes — including code comments, the GDD §4.4.3/§4.4.4 power-up section
   (following the "Thorn Field visibility + recharge" precedent, which documents
   the aura and cue beside the mechanics), `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`
   for the new cue, and any relevant README or wiki entries.
10. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity is mandatory.** No divergent copy: shared behaviour in
  `src/scenes/core/` (and shared dispatchers), consumed by `PlayScene` and every
  gym scene. Any intentional divergence must be recorded in this work item and in
  a code comment.
- **Audio goes through the cue pipeline.** A cue may not be synthesised ad hoc:
  it needs a `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` entry plus a recipe under
  `audio/toneforge/recipes/`, and (for `baked` delivery) a rebuilt WAV via
  `scripts/build-audio.sh`. The contract suite asserts every `play*` export is
  manifested.
- **No new runtime dependencies.**
- Cosmetic/feel work only — do **not** re-tune strike damage, interval or drop
  weight as part of this change unless a tuning defect is found (record it as
  linked follow-up work instead).
- CHANGELOG.md is excluded (managed by the ship release pipeline).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `onOrbitalStrike`: replace the generic
  `spawnNovaRing` composition with the new bolt VFX and the new cue.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — `_updateOrbitalStrike`: retain/requeue a
  bolt when no target or no player is available (the no-silent-waste seam).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `updateStrike`: expose a requeue/retain path so a
  decided bolt is not lost.
- `src/vfx/orbitalStrike.ts` — **New.** Descending bolt + impact-flash VFX,
  registered like `src/vfx/thornsAbsorb.ts` / `aoeEffect.ts`.
- `src/vfx/orbitalStrike.test.ts` — **New.** VFX composition/distinctness tests.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — **New** `playOrbitalStrikeSound` wrapper.
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` + `audio/toneforge/recipes/` — **New** cue
  entry (`aihell-orbital-strike`) and recipe.
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — document the new cue row.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — `next in Ns` countdown on the permanent `strike` row (AC6).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4.3/§4.4.4 power-up section: strike
  visibility + cue paragraph.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts` — gym parity + observability test.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (now confirmed):** "Orbital Strike" in the report means the
  **power-up** (`POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.strike`, display name exactly "Orbital
  Strike"), not the Missile-Command `orbital-strike` **hazard**. Confirmed by the
  producer (Q1 → (a)); the hazard is out of scope except for non-regression
  (AC7). Rationale: the hazard already has a telegraph, a falling shell, a
  detonation burst and a borrowed cue, whereas the power-up has no cue at all.
- **Risk — new audio asset cost.** A new dedicated recipe plus a WAV rebuild is
  required (Q2 → new strike SFX). This is the largest single risk: the ToneForge
  recipe must be authored, baked and manifested, and the baked asset must survive
  the audio balance guard. Budgeted as its own WBS item.
- **Risk — VFX legibility vs. visual noise.** A full-height bolt on every pulse
  may fight other screen effects; cap its draw to the target column and keep the
  duration short, and validate in `GymPowerUpsCombat` with a live player.
- **Risk — retarget semantics.** Retaining a queued bolt could stack up several
  bolts during a long enemy-free gap. AC3 caps the retained queue at one bolt (a
  permanent strike simply resumes its interval) so the behaviour stays
  predictable and testable.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Levelling, drop-weight and interval tuning, a strike
  "charging" telegraph, and multi-target strikes are all tempting; they are
  **out of scope** and should be captured as linked follow-up work items rather
  than absorbed here.
- **Assumption:** the "[no] VFX" complaint refers to the *generic, unnoticeable*
  ring rather than a rendering defect — no rendering bug was found in research.

## Related work

- **Some power-ups appear to do nothing (AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z)** — wired this
  power-up's gameplay consumers (commit `154b7adb`); AC5 covered damage only, not
  VFX/SFX.
- **Orbital Strike substrate (AH-0MVCRC1Q0007JAV1)** — catalogue, level curves,
  effects-registry accessors and HUD readouts for the net-new power-ups.
- **Missile Command telegraphed orbital strike (AH-0MV01ENX00055CG1)** — the
  unrelated enemy hazard (`src/entities/OrbitalStrike.ts`); reviewed for
  non-regression only.
- **Orbital-Strike falling shell projectile identity (AH-0MV822GIO005B685)** —
  the hazard projectile's visual identity; a useful precedent for giving the
  power-up its own identity.
- **Create E4 Phaser gym scene (AH-0MT99K3FE008CT13)** / Phaser orbital work —
  unrelated (`orbital` formation kind, not this power-up).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.3 (power-up levels, Orbital Strike row) and
  the "Thorn Field visibility + recharge" paragraph in the same section — the
  documentation precedent for describing a power-up's VFX/SFX.
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — the cue catalogue the new sound must
  join.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 — gym↔game parity convention.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Which "Orbital Strike" does this report mean: the power-up or the
  campaign hazard?**
  Options: (a) the **power-up** (`strike`, "Orbital Strike" pickup/choice
  reward); (b) the Missile-Command **hazard** (`orbital-strike` enemy entity);
  (c) both.
  **Recommended:** (a) the power-up — it has literally no SFX and only a
  borrowed generic AOE ring, which matches "no VFX or SFX".
  — **Answer (producer): (a) the power-up** — the `strike` power-up
  ("Orbital Strike"). Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-28. The Missile-Command
  `orbital-strike` **hazard** is therefore **out of scope**, reviewed for
  non-regression only (AC7). Research evidence supporting the answer: the
  power-up has zero audio cues and a generic 0.5 s ring; the hazard has a
  telegraph, a falling shell, a detonation burst and the borrowed
  `playScoutAdvanceCue`.

- **Q2 — May we add a new baked SFX cue, or must we reuse an existing one?**
  Options: (a) **new dedicated recipe** (`aihell-orbital-strike`) + baked WAV via
  `scripts/build-audio.sh`; (b) **reuse an existing electric recipe** (e.g.
  `aihell-arc-fire`) with no new asset; (c) no new audio, make the visual carry
  the identity.
  **Recommended:** (a) a new dedicated recipe — an orbital strike is a signature
  event and should not share a cue with the arc weapon.
  — **Answer (producer): a new dedicated strike SFX cue** — option (a). Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-10-28. Binding constraint: the cue needs a new ToneForge
  recipe (proposed slug `aihell-orbital-strike`) plus a baked WAV built via
  `scripts/build-audio.sh`; `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`,
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` and the audio contract tests
  (`src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts`, `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts`) must be
  updated in the same change.

- **Q3 — Should the permanent strike's HUD row show a countdown to the next
  bolt?**
  Options: (a) yes, add `next in Ns`; (b) no, keep the row as-is.
  **Recommended:** (a) yes — a 10–30 s interval is otherwise invisible, and the
  HUD already renders countdowns for other timed effects.
  — **Answer (producer): (a) yes** — add a `next in Ns` countdown to the
  permanent strike's HUD row. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-28. AC6 is now a
  required criterion rather than an optional one.

- **Q4 — Is it acceptable that the strike retains a queued bolt when no enemy is
  alive (rather than being wasted)?**
  **Recommended:** yes — silently losing a rare pickup is the reported bug.
  — **Answer (producer): yes, retain the bolt** — a queued bolt is retained and
  lands on the first frame with a valid target. Source: interactive reply,
  2026-10-28. AC3 is now the retention behaviour (retarget), not the alternative
  "signal as unused" path.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z** – Some power-ups appear to do nothing (completed)
- **AH-0MV01ENX00055CG1** – Missile Command telegraphed orbital strike (completed)

- `README.md` — matched: anything, don, fact, nothing, orbital (+5 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: doing, don, fact, nothing, orbital (+4 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: don, fact, nothing, orbital, sfx (+3 more)

Test-first verification slice for the scripted-video arc (parent AH-0MVPJ3NSK008V5VB; covers parent AC5 and the determinism half of AC4). This item writes the failing tests that specify the new scene-`setup` fields and the seven-beat example table **before** any implementation lands, so the behaviour is pinned by tests rather than by prose.

- **AC1 — New setup fields are parsed and validated.** `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` covers `setup.player.weaponLevels`, `setup.bossHitsRemaining` and `setup.mineralReward`: accepted shapes parse; wrong shapes raise the documented error codes; normalisation yields documented defaults; re-normalising a normalised setup is idempotent (deep-equal).

Out-of-range values (e.g. `0`, negative, non-integer, above the entity's total HP) are rejected with a documented code.

Scene 6 (reprise) is asserted to differ from scene 4 in both enemy mix and player weapons, so a copy-paste edit cannot collapse the two beats.

## Goal / user story

`GymPowerUpsUtility`, `GymWeaponLeveling`, `GymWeapons`

## Goal

As a player, picking up an Orbital Strike when no enemy is alive should not waste it — the bolt waits and lands on the next valid target — so a rare pickup is never silently consumed.

## Parent

AH-0MVRE6N08001TE4V — Orbital Strike does nothing (AC3).

## Context

Two silent-failure paths exist today:

- **No target:** `EffectsRegistry.updateStrike(dt)` (`src/powerups/effects.ts:1241`) clears `_strikePulsePending` before the scene knows whether a bolt can be resolved; `CombatScene.onOrbitalStrike` then returns early when no live enemy exists (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:646`) — the pickup is gone with zero feedback.
- **No player:** `CombatCoreScene._updateOrbitalStrike` (`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts:1655`) does not guard on a live player; `onOrbitalStrike` does the same early return.

This item makes "a bolt is due" a **latched** decision that is only cleared once the bolt is actually resolved, so it is retried every frame until it lands. The producer confirmed retention over "signal as unused" (Appendix Q4) and that at most **one** bolt may be retained (Appendix Q4 / AC3).

## Deliverables

- `src/powerups/effects.ts`: replace the consume-on-read behaviour of `updateStrike(dt)` with a **latch** — a due bolt stays due until the shared core resolves it (e.g. `updateStrike` reports due without clearing, plus a `resolveStrike()` acknowledgement; while a bolt is latched the permanent interval timer does not advance and does not bank further bolts). Document the semantics in JSDoc.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`: `_updateOrbitalStrike` only acknowledges the latch when the bolt actually resolved — i.e. `onOrbitalStrike` returns a boolean (resolved / could-not-resolve) and the core acknowledges on `true`. With no player or no live enemy it returns `false` and the bolt stays latched for the next frame.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`: `onOrbitalStrike` returns `true` only after it has applied the bolt (nearest target found and damaged); returns `false` when there is no player or no live enemy.
- Scene reset (`_resetRunState` / registry reset) clears any latched bolt so a restart starts clean.
- Regression tests: pickup with no live enemy → bolt retained → lands on the next live enemy; pickup with no live player → retained; a long enemy-free gap banks at most one bolt; a permanent strike's interval resumes normally after a retained bolt lands.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **No silent waste.** A strike that resolves while no live enemy (or no live player) is present is retained and lands on the next target — at most one bolt is retained.
- The retention lives in shared code (`src/powerups/effects.ts` state + `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` acknowledgement), so `PlayScene` and every gym inherit it with no scene-specific copy.
- A scene reset (`_resetRunState`) clears a latched bolt — no bolt survives a restart into a fresh run.
- Bolt resolution still applies damage exactly once per landed bolt (no double damage from retries).
- `/skill:test` (changed scope) passes.

## Constraints

- Do not change the strike **interval** or **damage** values — only when a decided bolt is consumed.
- Keep the fingerprint of the public registry API minimal and documented; `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.test.ts` and `src/scenes/core/enemyForceFieldDamageSources.test.ts` drive `updateStrike` and must stay green (update their call sites if the API gains an acknowledgement step).
- Precision: retrying must be frame-driven (dt-based), not timer/sleep driven, so tests stay deterministic.

- Parent AC3: **No silent waste.** A strike that resolves while no live enemy (or no live player) is present is **not** lost: the queued bolt is **retained** and lands on the first frame with a valid target ... At most one bolt is retained (a permanent strike simply resumes its interval) so a long enemy-free gap cannot bank a volley.

## What to build

1. A new pure module `src/waves/campaignVariety.ts` (no Phaser/runtime import) exporting:

implementation is driven by tests rather than retrofitted. The tests live in

  verified by an exhaustive slot-index sweep (no statistical tolerance).

  picks (one owned kind landing a 3-slot gains +3 levels on it).
- **Bonus** — the bonus outcome grants +1 level to **every** owned permanent
  kind.
- **Pool coverage** — owned kinds come from the shared six-slot accounting, so
  the tests cover both halves of the shared pool (power-up kinds and weapon
  drops) and never include the permanent cannon or the `reset` utility.
- **Determinism** — the same run seed plus the same owned-kind snapshot
  reproduces the same outcome; a source-scan assertion proves the module
  contains no `Math.random()` and no wall-clock read.
- **Purity** — the module imports neither Phaser nor any scene module.

committed **first** (failing for the right reason, recorded in an item

# Continue not navigatable in menu (AH-0MVSHH20J003YXDN)

## Problem statement

In the main menu, the **Continue — Level N** control (shown when a saved
checkpoint exists, AH-0MVCRBTNF000DK51) cannot be reached with the keyboard:
Tab / arrow keys skip it, so Enter/Space can never activate it. The mouse
works. This breaks the keyboard-only control guarantee (GDD §2.1: *"no mouse
is ever required"*) for the most prominent menu option.

Root cause: `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts::create()` pushes the Continue text into
`this.controls` (used only by `getFocusedLabel()` for test/label lookup) but
**never registers it with the shared `FocusManager`** — every other control
is registered via `this.focusManager.register(...)`. The button was added
post-keyboard-support in commit `a8afdecc`.

## Users

Players who navigate the menu by keyboard only; accessibility users; and
anyone resuming a run who expects the *primary* action (Continue) to be the
natural default choice.

**User stories**

- As a keyboard-only player, I want to reach **Continue** with Tab/ArrowDown
  and activate it with Enter, so that I can resume my run without a mouse.
- As a player resuming a run, I want **Continue** to be the default focused
  control while a checkpoint exists, so that pressing Enter immediately
  resumes my run (consistent with conventional game-menu UX).
- As a keyboard-only player, I want focus never to wrap to the bottom
  dev button when navigating the menu, so that arrow navigation follows
  on-screen order.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Continue is keyboard-reachable and the default focus when a
  checkpoint exists.** When a resumable checkpoint is present, the Continue
  button is registered with the shared `FocusManager` as the *first* control,
  so it is focused by default (visible focus highlight, matching the
  established pattern) and cycling forward reaches it before Play Game.
  *Verification:* unit test boots `MenuScene` with a seeded checkpoint and
  asserts `getFocusedLabel()` equals the Continue label without any key
  press.
- **AC2 — Tab/arrow cycling follows on-screen visual order.** With a
  checkpoint absent, the existing order is unchanged (Play Game first, Tab
  wraps back to Play Game). With a checkpoint present, cycling order is
  **Continue → Play Game → Watch Demo → Settings → Leaderboard → GitHub →
  Gym Scene Index (dev)**, wrapping at both ends (ArrowUp on the dev button
  lands on GitHub, never skipping). *Verification:* unit test emits Tab and
  ArrowUp/ArrowDown sequences with a seeded checkpoint and asserts the
  visited labels and wrap behaviour.
- **AC3 — Enter/Space on a focused Continue resumes the run identically to a
  click.** Activation calls the same code path as the pointerdown handler
  (`resumeAudioContext` + `scene.start('PlayScene', { demo: false,
  resume: true })`), restoring the saved level/state. Focus stays on Continue
  after activation. *Verification:* unit test focuses Continue, presses
  Enter, and asserts `PlayScene` is active at the saved wave/level with its
  restored stats (reuse the existing AC3/AC4 resume assertions).
- **AC4 — No pointer/regression changes outside the Continue registration.**
  Mouse behaviour (hover highlight, pointerdown resume) is unchanged; all
  existing MenuScene keyboard and control-count tests remain green with no
  checkpoint present.
- **AC5 — Keyboard tests added/updated.** `src/scenes/MenuScene.test.ts` gains
  tests for AC1–AC3 in the checkpoint-Continue describe block; the existing
  no-checkpoint keyboard tests are unchanged.
- **AC6 — Docs updated.** GDD §2.1 *Menu & UI navigation (keyboard)* is
  updated so the menu paragraph reflects reality: with a checkpoint,
  **Continue** is focused by default and the Tab order includes **Continue**
  (and the **GitHub** link, which the same paragraph currently omits); the
  `MenuScene` module doc-comment is updated to describe the Continue
  registration.
- **AC7 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site
  entries.
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing shared `FocusManager` (`src/utils/focusManager.ts`) —
  do **not** add ad-hoc key handling; no `FocusManager` API changes.
- The Continue control is shown only when a usable checkpoint exists —
  no checkpoint behaviour changes (AH-0MVCRBTNF000DK51 AC3).
- Difficulty chosen by the operator: **minimal fix** — register Continue with
  the same activate callback as its `pointerdown` handler; a broader
  "every control must be registered" parity guard was explicitly **not**
  requested.
- Keyboard support is **additive**: pointer handlers stay intact.
- No CI/CD pipeline tests (per intake convention).

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts::create()` renders Continue (y=170) above Play
  Game (y=220) when `loadCheckpoint()` returns a checkpoint. It
  `setInteractive`s the text, wires hover + `pointerdown` (resume), pushes
  `{ label, text }` into `this.controls`, but calls `this.focusManager.register`
  for **every other** control (Play Game, Watch Demo, Settings, Leaderboard,
  GitHub, Gym Scene Index) before `attachKeyboard(this)`.
- `FocusManager.register` focuses its first registered control by default
  (AC2 of AH-0MUBZT64O0056BRY) and paints focus/unfocus styles.
- GDD §2.1 menu paragraph is stale: it documents *"Play Game is focused by
  default"* and lists the Tab cycle as *Play Game → Watch Demo → Settings →
  Leaderboard → Gym Scene Index (dev)* — omitting both Continue and the
  GitHub footer link.
- Existing keyboard tests in `src/scenes/MenuScene.test.ts` assert a
  6-control cycle with Play Game as default (no checkpoint in those tests,
  so they still hold).

## Desired change

In `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts::create()`:

1. Register Continue with the shared focus manager immediately after building
   it, before Play Game, so it becomes the first (default-focused) control and
   sits first in the Tab cycle:
   ```ts
   this.focusManager.register(continueButton, () => {
     resumeAudioContext(this.sound);
     this.scene.start('PlayScene', { demo: false, resume: true });
   });
   ```
2. Keep the existing `controls.push` (used by `getFocusedLabel()`).
3. No changes to the pointer handlers, Play Game, or the other controls.
4. Update the `MenuScene` module doc-comment keyboard paragraph, GDD §2.1
   (menu row) and the README menu/keyboard-only-navigation claims to state
   the checkpoint-dependent default focus and the full Tab order including
   Continue and GitHub.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` — register Continue with `FocusManager` as the
  first control; update the module doc-comment.
- `src/scenes/MenuScene.test.ts` — add AC1–AC3 keyboard tests in the
  checkpoint-Continue describe block.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — update §2.1 menu keyboard paragraph
  (default focus + full Tab order).
- `README.md` — update the checkpoint-dependent
  default-focus claims in the MenuScene scene list ("Play Game is focused by
  default") and the Keyboard-only navigation paragraph to state the Continue
  default focus and full Tab order when a checkpoint exists (AC7).

## Risks

- **Focus default flip.** With a checkpoint present, the default focus
  changes from Play Game to Continue — intended per Q1 (a), but a behaviour
  change worth confirming during review; no test asserts Play Game as default
  when a checkpoint exists.
- **Stale-doc drift.** The GDD §2.1 Tab-cycle text is already out of date
  (missing GitHub); scope here is limited to adding Continue (+ GitHub in the
  same sentence) — a fuller docs audit is a separate task.
- **Scope creep.** A blanket "every control must be registered" guard test
  was considered and declined by the operator (Q3 (a)); do not add it.

## Assumptions

- **Checkpoint presence drives both default focus and Tab order.** Continue
  is registered as the first control only when a checkpoint exists; with no
  checkpoint the menu behaves exactly as today (Play Game default, 6-control
  cycle).
- Visual order == Tab order (Continue is drawn at y=170, above Play Game).
- Continue's activation is identical for pointer and keyboard (single shared
  callback closed over the button, as with the other controls).
- Focus styling uses `FocusManager` defaults; Continue's base `#88ffff`
  becomes the unfocused `#00ffff` when another control gains focus and the
  focus highlight when focused — consistent with every other control.
- The capture tooling is unaffected: `captureStartKeys('demo')` presses a
  single Tab to reach Watch Demo, which stays valid because every batch
  item runs on a fresh page/context with no checkpoint.

## Related work

- AH-0MVCRBTNF000DK51 — Checkpoint save/resume. *Completed — introduced the
  Continue button that was never keyboard-registered (commit `a8afdecc`).*
- AH-0MU9LKQEP008LCX9 — Keyboard only control (umbrella). *Completed.*
- AH-0MUBZT64O0056BRY — Reusable in-canvas focus manager (core utility).
  *Completed — the utility this fix uses.*
- AH-0MUBZTFR4001JLF3 — MenuScene keyboard support. *Completed — the
  registration pattern to follow.*
- AH-0MUDZFBYY008P7ZE — Gym scenes index not navigable by keyboard.
  *Completed — same class of bug (a control missing from keyboard navigation),
  resolved the same way; useful precedent.*
- AH-0MUBZTZ7P00838MH — Keyboard-driven scene navigation tests. *Completed.*
- AH-0MUBZUH6K009WXWO — Documentation updates for keyboard navigation.
  *Completed — updated GDD §2.1 previously (pre-Continue/GitHub).*
- AH-0MUZI83EO003WVTG — Add a GitHub link to the main menu. *Completed — the
  other control omitted from the GDD §2.1 Tab-cycle text.*

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1:** "When a checkpoint exists, should Continue be the default focused
  control (option a) or should Play Game keep the default focus (option b)?"
  — **Answer (operator):** (a) — Continue focused by default. Source:
  interactive reply (session herdr-1793214823-2995051-31375).
- **Q2:** "When Continue is visible, should Tab/arrow order be visual order
  (Continue first, option a) or keep Play Game first and append Continue
  (option b)?" — **Answer (operator):** (a) — visual order, Continue first.
  Source: interactive reply (same session).
- **Q3:** "Scope: minimal fix (register Continue + regression tests + GDD §2.1
  refresh, option a) or also add a guard test asserting every interactive
  control is focus-registered (option b)?" — **Answer (operator):** (a) —
  minimal fix only; no guard test. Source: interactive reply (same session).
